message.text:
Explicit Go and SQL code removes emoji reactions when a user is deleted. DELETE statements target the reaction table by content_id and creator_id.

Checking user_delete.go across all three database drivers. Also verifying whether a foreign key cascade exists at the schema level.
Explicit DELETE statements showed up in the MySQL user-delete path; I'll confirm the other drivers and whether the schema also cascades.
Checking the reaction table schema for foreign keys. Tracing the delete user flow through related functions. Verifying whether the API layer handles reactions.

Reactions are removed by explicit Go code. The reaction table lacks a foreign key or ON DELETE CASCADE constraint. The deletion logic issues DELETE SQL statements directly.

All three database drivers follow the same deletion pattern.

h05.
explicit Go code; `store/db/mysql/user_delete.go`, `store/db/sqlite/user_delete.go`, `store/db/postgres/user_delete.go` (no FK/CASCADE in `store/migration/*/LATEST.sql`)

`DeleteUser` in each driver deletes reactions in-process: `deleteReactionsByContentIDsTx` (`DELETE FROM reaction WHERE content_id IN …`) and `deleteReactionsByCreatorTx` (`DELETE FROM reaction WHERE creator_id = …`). MySQL calls them at `store/db/mysql/user_delete.go:96` and `:102`; SQLite/Postgres have the same helpers (~lines 383 and 401). The `reaction` table in `store/migration/{sqlite,mysql,postgres}/LATEST.sql` has `creator_id` as a plain column with a UNIQUE constraint and no `FOREIGN KEY` / `ON DELETE CASCADE`. The API (`server/router/api/v1/user_service.go`) only calls `Store.DeleteUser`.
